Anita: Heads-up: customers keep hitting ambiguity because SDKs return one opaque `APIError`. We should expose a tiny, consistent error surface so downstream code can make deterministic choices (retry vs show UI vs drop).

Leo: Agreed. Minimal set I like: AuthError, RateLimitError, ValidationError, SafetyRejectError, ServerTransientError. Each error should include `code`, `retryable` (bool), `retry_after` (secs opt), `hint` (short user-facing guidance), and `internal_id` for support.

Priya: For parity: python already returns specialized classes; JS should set `name` + `code` + `retryable` to avoid string parsing. Go should export interface `IsRetryable() bool` and typed errors for switch. We should add unit tests that assert the envelope fields exist.

Anita: UX note: sampleapp should show exact copy for each case (e.g. AuthError -> "Reconnect account", RateLimitError -> "You're sending requests too quickly; try again in N seconds"). Keep copy in a shared constants file.

Leo: Console needs a `signal` tag preserved for grouping (examples: `quota_exceeded`, `auth_expired`, `safety_blocked`). Helps triage and automated suggestions.

devex-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-517: "typed errors + parity tests + sampleapp error flows" and linked this thread.

Anita: I'll draft a tiny RFC with example JSON envelope and PR checklist (js/go/python), include sampleapp snippets. Will ping when ready.

Priya: Thanks. I'll add tests to CI so parity doesn't regress.
